vendor_company: Cin7 (formerly DEAR Systems brand; acquired and rebranded under Cin7)
hq_country: United States (Denver, Colorado; originally New Zealand)
target_vertical: Multi-channel retailer, light manufacturer, wholesaler, DTC brand
pricing_model: Tiered SaaS subscription with caps on users, integrations, and annual order volume; add-on modules (WMS, B2B Portal, Automation, Production, ForesightAI in some tiers)
shopify_sync_direction: Bi-directional for orders and products; inventory is one-way push from Cin7 Core to Shopify only (Cin7 Core is the source of truth for stock).
shopify_synced_entities: Products, variants, inventory (stock levels push Core->Shopify), orders, customers, fulfillments, payments, returns/refunds, and product images. Stock is pushed Core->Shopify only; product info can be pushed or downloaded.
shopify_service_item_support: [uncertain] — Cin7 Core supports non-inventory/service products in its own catalogue, but explicit handling of Shopify service-type items in 2025/2026 is not clearly documented
shopify_multi_store_support: Yes — multiple Shopify stores can be linked to a single Cin7 Core tenant; each consumes one integration licence and has independent catalog/settings.
shopify_pos_support: Shopify POS orders flow through the Shopify integration like online orders; Cin7 Core also has its own POS module. Native POS-specific feature depth is limited.
shopify_b2b_catalog_support: Limited native support — Cin7 Core can pass B2B pricing/customers to a Shopify B2B-configured store, but deep Shopify B2B (company locations, catalogs, price lists) typically uses partner apps like SparkLayer.
shopify_markets_support: [uncertain] — no explicit documentation found of dedicated Shopify Markets (multi-market pricing/duties/landed cost) handling
shopify_metafield_to_erp_field_mapping: [uncertain] — generic metafield<->custom field mapping is not a documented feature; mapping is largely fixed to standard fields
shopify_variant_option_mapping: Variants map via SKU; Cin7 Core product families/variants align to Shopify variants. SKU is the primary key for matching listings and inventory.
shopify_real_time_or_batch: Event-driven near real-time via Shopify webhooks for orders and via Core push on stock changes; product list/relist can be manual or auto-trigger.
shopify_known_limitations: Inventory sync is one-way only (Core->Shopify); cannot push stock from Shopify back to Core. Variants must match by SKU. Heavier B2B (Plus) and Markets features require partner apps. Users report sync delays/failures during peak, limited handling of bundles when Shopify treats them as single SKUs, and complaints around partial fulfillments and edge cases in returns. Each Shopify store consumes one integration licence.
etsy_native_or_third_party: Native direct Etsy integration (Cin7 Core connects directly to the Etsy API).
etsy_listing_creation_vs_sync_only: Primarily sync-focused — Cin7 Core can download existing Etsy listings and map them to Core products, push price/stock updates, and renew inactive listings; native creation of brand-new Etsy listings from Core is limited compared with Shopify.
etsy_inventory_sync: Stock levels push from Core to Etsy on changes; manual mode available; auto-renew of out-of-stock (inactive) listings is supported.
etsy_order_import: Orders download from Etsy to Cin7 Core automatically based on configured capture status.
etsy_synced_entities: Listings (download/map), inventory, orders, customers, payments. Variations supported via SKU matching.
etsy_known_limitations: Personalization fields and digital-product nuances are not deeply modelled; mapping relies heavily on SKU and can miss variations without consistent SKUs; listing creation from Core is limited.
amazon_marketplaces: US, CA, MX, UK, DE, ES, FR, IT, NL, SE, BE, PL, UAE, AU, JP, IN, SG, ZA (Africa). Multiple marketplaces per region supported.
amazon_seller_types: FBM and FBA (FBA as an external fulfillment location); Vendor Central is not natively supported.
amazon_synced_entities: Listings (link by SKU/ASIN), inventory levels (Core->Amazon), orders, customers, payments, settlement fees, and shipment/tracking from FBA.
amazon_listing_creation: Sync/link existing listings primarily; full listing creation/management is limited — typically requires existing ASIN/listing in Seller Central.
amazon_repricing_support: Not included; relies on third-party repricer tools.
amazon_buy_shipping: [uncertain] — not a documented native feature (Veeqo-style in-app Amazon Buy Shipping)
amazon_fba_inbound_workflow: FBA inbound shipment creation is NOT supported natively in Cin7 Core; FBA is modelled as an external fulfillment location with stock-level auto-sync (daily/weekly/monthly) and order/fulfillment flow. Inbound shipment creation is on the roadmap per Cin7 support.
amazon_sp_api_inbound_v2024_03_20: [uncertain] — no public statement confirming migration to Fulfillment Inbound API v2024-03-20; FBA inbound is not currently supported anyway
amazon_settlement_report_handling: Cin7 Core can capture and automatically process Amazon Settlements Reports (typically issued at ~2-week intervals). Users map Amazon fee categories (commission, FBA fees, shipping fees, refunds) to Chart of Accounts expense accounts; the settlement is posted as a consolidated transaction with line items per fee type. Can also be processed manually.
amazon_marketplace_facilitator_tax_handl: For Marketplace Facilitator (MPF) jurisdictions where Amazon collects/remits tax, Cin7 (Omni explicitly, Core comparably) does not download the MPF-collected tax onto the sales order so it is not double-counted in tax liabilities.
amazon_multi_account_support: Multiple Amazon seller accounts can be connected per Cin7 Core tenant, subject to integration licence limits of the plan.
amazon_known_limitations: No FBA inbound shipment creation; no Vendor Central; no native repricer; FBA stock sync interval can be daily/weekly/monthly rather than truly real-time; listing creation/management depth is limited; mapping relies on SKU/ASIN; community reports issues around multi-marketplace SKU collisions and settlement edge cases.
xero_app_store_certified: Listed on Xero App Store (certified integration).
xero_app_awards_recognition: Cin7 named a finalist in the Xero Global App Awards 2025 (Australia region).
xero_app_store_rating: Approximately 4 out of 5 stars based on ~228 reviews on the Xero App Store (figure as of 2025 reporting; current count may vary).
xero_synced_entities: Invoices (sales), bills (purchases), payments, contacts (customers and suppliers), credit notes, inventory adjustments via journals, COGS journals, chart of accounts, tax rules, payment terms, and tracking categories.
xero_accounting_sync_mode: Hybrid — supports both per-invoice posting and consolidated/summary transactions (e.g. daily summary journals) configurable by user. Cin7 Core acts as the inventory source of truth and posts financial impacts to Xero.
xero_cogs_journal_method: Perpetual per-movement COGS journals (COGS posted on each shipment/fulfillment) with landed-cost-inclusive valuation when landed costs are allocated to receipts/production.
xero_multi_currency: Yes — multi-currency invoice and bill posting supported (must align with Xero's multi-currency edition).
xero_tracking_category_mapping: Maps up to Xero's two active tracking categories; values can be mapped from Cin7 Core fields (e.g. location, sales rep, brand, customer category) and are populated on transactions at sync.
xero_tax_handling: Tax codes (GST/VAT/sales tax) imported from Xero during initial sync and mapped onto Core tax rules; transactions sync with mapped tax codes.
xero_known_limitations: Limit of 2 Xero tracking categories. Base currency of Core must match Xero base currency. Re-mapping the chart of accounts after go-live can be painful. Historical/large catch-up syncs can be slow. Some users report issues with credit notes, refunds, and reconciling consolidated postings.
qb_desktop_supported: No — QuickBooks Desktop is not supported.
qb_app_certified: Listed on the Intuit QuickBooks App Store; Intuit has cited Cin7 as a preferred inventory integration.
qb_synced_entities: Invoices, bills, payments, customers, vendors, products/items, inventory adjustments, COGS journals, credit memos, chart of accounts, tax codes.
qb_accounting_sync_mode: Hybrid — supports per-document posting and a 'no sync' option for consolidated reconciliation; configurable.
qb_cogs_journal_method: Perpetual per-movement COGS journals with landed-cost-inclusive valuation when landed costs are applied to receipts/production.
qb_multi_currency: Yes — multi-currency supported provided Core base currency matches QBO base currency and QBO multi-currency is enabled.
qb_class_location_mapping: Supports mapping to QBO Class and Location dimensions analogous to Xero tracking categories.
qb_known_limitations: Requires QuickBooks Online Plus or Advanced (Simple Start and Essentials are not supported / not fully functional); Core base currency must match QBO base currency; no QBO Desktop; reconciling consolidated summary postings can take effort; historical syncs of large datasets are slow.
other_ecom_channels: WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Magento (native), eBay (native), Walmart Marketplace, TikTok Shop, Squarespace (via partners), Wix (via partners), Faire/JOOR (via direct and partner), Square, plus integrations with Shopify and Etsy already listed.
bundle_kit_component_decomposition: Yes — Assembly BOMs support kits/bundles where component stock decrements on assembly (and can be reversed via disassembly). Auto-assembly logic decrements components at fulfillment.
other_accounting_integrations: Limited beyond Xero and QBO — partner/iPaaS integrations exist for Sage Intacct, NetSuite, and others via tools like Pipe17 or custom API work; no broad native list of MYOB/Sage 50/Zoho Books/FreshBooks native connectors in Core (some via partners).
bom_support: Yes — robust BOM module (Assembly BOM and Production BOM).
multi_level_bom: Yes — multi-level/nested BOMs supported; Production BOM Explosion / Nested Production Orders allow sub-assemblies to be produced on demand.
production_orders: Yes — both Assembly Orders (light kitting/packing) and Production Orders (multi-step manufacturing with routings, by-products, semi-finished tracking, third-party manufacturing). MRP suggests production and purchase orders from demand.
batch_lot_tracking: Yes — batch number tracking with expiry dates and lot-recall traceability reports.
serial_tracking: Yes — full serial number tracking, including in WMS pick flows.
bin_location_support: Yes — bins are the smallest WMS storage unit; multi-bin locations per warehouse with put-away and pick logic.
barcoding: Yes — barcode generation, label printing (configurable templates), and barcode scanning via the WMS app and supported scanners.
purchase_orders: Yes — full PO lifecycle with partial receipts, drop-shipping, blind receipts, supplier price lists, and conversion to bills.
supplier_management: Yes — supplier records, supplier-product mapping (supplier SKU, supplier price), lead times, default suppliers; MOQs supported via reorder configuration.
landed_cost_support: Yes — strong landed-cost engine: freight, insurance, duty, and other costs allocated to inventory cost by total cost, quantity, weight, or volume (or manually). Allocations supported on purchases, stock transfers, adjustments, assemblies, and production runs.
multi_currency_inventory_valuation: Inventory is valued in the Cin7 Core base currency; purchases in foreign currencies are converted at FX into the base for valuation (no per-currency valuation layer).
ai_demand_forecasting: Yes — Cin7 ForesightAI (built into Core and Omni). Combines statistical methods with proprietary AI/ML for demand forecasts up to 24 months ahead; underpinned by acquisition of Inventoro.
ai_purchase_order_suggestions: Yes — Smart Reorder and Smart Buyer suggest PO drafts and replenishment based on ForesightAI predicted demand, lead times, and safety stock.
ai_natural_language_query: Yes — 'Ask Me Anything' (AMA) natural-language insights tool launched/expanded in August 2025 across all Cin7 versions; returns answers as tables, graphs, downloadable graphics, or CSV.
public_api: Yes — public REST API (Cin7 Core API V1 and V2, documented at dearinventory.docs.apiary.io). Good coverage of products, orders, purchases, inventory, BOMs, manufacturing, contacts; sandboxed and widely used by partners.
webhook_event_coverage: Webhooks available (requires the Automation add-on module); cover sale, purchase, stock adjustment, product, and assembly events. Subscription is via API POST.
integration_architecture: Mostly native first-party integrations for major channels and accounting (Shopify, Amazon, Etsy, eBay, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Magento, Xero, QBO, ShipStation), supplemented by partner-built and iPaaS connectors (Patchworks, Pipe17, Celigo) and Zapier/Make for long-tail apps.
zapier_make_support: Yes — official Zapier integration; Make (formerly Integromat) supported.
mobile_app: Yes — Cin7 Core WMS app for iOS and Android (and a Sales/POS-focused app variant); used for inventory operations, picking, packing, receiving, put-away, stock counts, and barcode scanning.
mobile_barcode_scanning_app: Yes — native barcode scanning in the WMS app via Bluetooth scanners (ScanSKU, mPOP recommended) or device camera (iOS 15+/Android 5.1+).
rate_limit_handling_documented: Cin7 Core's own API rate limits are documented (request caps with throttling). Public documentation on how the platform handles Shopify/Amazon/Xero/QBO downstream rate limits is limited beyond general statements about retries/queues.
sync_frequency: Shopify/WooCommerce/BigCommerce/Etsy/eBay: near real-time via webhooks for orders and event-driven push for stock changes from Core. Amazon FBA stock auto-sync: daily/weekly/monthly. Xero/QBO: per-event or scheduled (configurable). Some partner integrations (e.g. JOOR) run every 60 minutes.
shipping_carrier_integrations: Direct carrier integrations are largely delivered via shipping services (ShipStation, Shippit, EasyPost, Starshipit, Sendle, AusPost MyPost Business, etc.) which import carriers automatically; some direct integrations (e.g. USPS via EasyPost, AusPost, FedEx, UPS, DHL via shipping services).
shipping_label_buying: Yes — in-app label purchase is supported via integrated shipping services (e.g. ShipStation as a Shipping Service, EasyPost), allowing rate shopping and label printing from inside a Cin7 Core sale.
three_pl_integrations: Native integrations with ShipBob and ShipHero; FBA modelled as a 3PL location; additional 3PLs supported via Pipe17, Extensiv, and EDI/API integrations.
edi_support: Yes — EDI supported via partners and Cin7's marketplace; commonly used for big-box retail (e.g. via SPS Commerce, Crossfire, B2BGateway-style integrations).
g2_rating: Approximately 4.1/5 across ~445 reviews on G2 (Cin7 product family; as of 2025/2026).
capterra_rating: Approximately 4.3-4.5/5 across ~290-300 reviews on Capterra (figures vary slightly by snapshot).
notable_customers: Multiple SMB and growth-stage brands across DTC, apparel, food and beverage, electronics, and wholesale; Cin7 reports thousands of customers across 90+ countries. Specific public case studies include consumer brands featured on cin7.com (e.g. various apparel, food, beauty brands).
last_major_release: August 2025 — expansion of AI capabilities including the 'Ask Me Anything' tool included at no extra cost; ForesightAI enhancements announced at Summit 2025 (Sep/Oct 2025).
owner_parent_company: Cin7 (parent of the Core product since the 2021 acquisition/rebranding of DEAR Systems). Cin7 is majority-owned by Rubicon Technology Partners (US private equity).
last_funding_event: November 2024 — Rubicon Technology Partners closed a $500M single-asset continuation fund to extend its investment in Cin7, with CVC Secondary Partners as lead and participation from Ares, BlackRock, Goldman Sachs AM, and Schroders Capital. Initial Rubicon majority investment was in 2019 (~$133M). Cin7 acquired AI forecasting company Inventoro to power ForesightAI.
public_status_page_uptime: https://status.cin7.com — publicly available; recent third-party trackers report variable uptime (e.g. 100% in Dec 2025/Jan 2026, but ~81-99% in some months; multiple incidents tracked over time).
